paper.title: What Matters in Humanoid General Motion Tracking? An Empirical Study
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-07-22; paper-linked official code hucebot/yahmp pinned at 2111a998663e9f787b3ac36e8f8a7c17745ca83f and inspected 2026-08-30; the paper does not assert commit-to-experiment identity

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It is a controlled G1 study showing that reference fields, temporal context, action centering, actuation, randomization, and training approach can materially or directionally change independent tracking metrics; it therefore defines confounds to freeze and a concrete evaluation protocol for Sam's two-knob harness.
not_evidence_for: A causal benefit from oracle or mode composition
The optimality or cross-task transfer of the fixed YAHMP reward coefficients
A gain under Sam's fixed trainer because several studied factors are trainer or controller changes
Factor interactions or generality beyond the Unitree G1
Statistically quantified multi-seed or sim-to-real reliability
Human-language steering or recursive harness improvement
Identity between the pinned public code commit and the code that produced every reported experiment

mechanisms.name: One-factor controlled variant protocol
mechanisms.description: A nominal G1 PPO pipeline is held fixed while one of six axes changes: motion command, observation history, action representation, actuation profile, hand-force randomization, or policy-training approach.

mechanisms.name: Reference-conditioned actor interface
mechanisms.description: The deployable actor receives proprioception, a current motion command with reference joint position and velocity plus base targets, and optionally a short command-state history.

mechanisms.name: Tracking-statistic clip and phase replay
mechanisms.description: Resets sample a motion and initial phase; training tracking statistics increase replay of poorly tracked clips and phases while a uniform component preserves coverage.

mechanisms.name: Fixed tracking and regularization reward
mechanisms.description: All variants share eight exponential tracking terms and four costs for force, slip, action rate, and joint-limit violations, keeping reward constant during the factor study.

mechanisms.name: Torque-feasible hand-force randomization
mechanisms.description: Training samples hand side, application point, duration, and cooldown, then caps forces for joint-torque feasibility to expose the policy to interaction loads absent from free-space tracking.

mechanisms.name: Privileged teacher with PPO-KL student
mechanisms.description: A privileged PPO teacher is frozen; a deployable student is then trained with PPO plus a KL penalty toward the teacher distribution.

failure_modes.name: Reference-velocity omission
failure_modes.description: Removing explicit reference joint velocity worsens every reported tracking metric by 7% to 15%, despite retaining observation history.

failure_modes.name: No-history degradation
failure_modes.description: Removing history worsens all six errors, with base-position and base-orientation mean errors rising 38% and 50%.

failure_modes.name: Stiff-profile torque and oscillation cost
failure_modes.description: The stiffer fixed-scale profile gives mixed tracking changes but raises simulated peak torque and produces more oscillatory hardware crouching.

failure_modes.name: Metric-direction reversal
failure_modes.description: Residual-action, actuation, and teacher-student variants improve some metrics while worsening others, so a single scalar score can conceal tradeoffs.

failure_modes.name: Single-platform one-factor scope
failure_modes.description: The study uses one robot and changes one factor at a time around one nominal pipeline; interactions and cross-platform transfer are unmeasured.

failure_modes.name: Source-dataset and subject overlap
failure_modes.description: Train and test clips are distinct after retargeting, but they may come from the same source datasets and human subjects.

failure_modes.name: Limited training-seed uncertainty
failure_modes.description: The authors state that one additional seed preserved trends, but the main table does not expose per-seed estimates or uncertainty across training runs.

failure_modes.name: Narrow success and hardware evidence
failure_modes.description: Simulation success is only absence of torso-ground contact; pushes, soft ground, and lifting are qualitative, while hand-load values come from one execution per policy.

evaluation.name: Held-out motion tracking protocol
evaluation.description: All policies run the same 1,024 disjoint retargeted motion clips at 50 Hz without perturbations; errors are averaged over time per motion before cross-motion aggregation.

evaluation.name: Six-metric tracking panel
evaluation.description: Base position/orientation, nine-body position/orientation, and joint position/velocity errors expose directionally mixed design tradeoffs independently of training reward.

evaluation.name: Actuation-effort evaluation
evaluation.description: Mean and maximum absolute torque are measured across all, upper-body, and lower-body joints to reveal costs not visible in tracking errors.

evaluation.name: TWIST2 common-protocol comparison
evaluation.description: TWIST2 is retrained on the same 11,151 motions and iteration count and evaluated on the same metrics, while remaining a complete-pipeline rather than single-factor baseline.

evaluation.name: Controlled hand-load test
evaluation.description: Matched policies hold the same right-arm configuration under progressive loads; steady-window elbow displacement measures interaction-force capability separately from free-space tracking.

evaluation.name: Zero-shot G1 hardware demonstration
evaluation.description: The same simulated checkpoint runs at 50 Hz without hardware fine-tuning or command smoothing for diverse motion replay, manual perturbations, and soft-ground double-support trials.

evidence.locator: arXiv metadata and abstract; submitted 22 July 2026
evidence.claim: The v1 paper introduces YAHMP and a controlled study of six general-motion-tracking design axes on the Unitree G1.

evidence.locator: Section II-B, Equations 1-3, and Table I
evidence.claim: The actor's proprioception, nominal reference command, and 0/10/20-step history variants are explicitly defined.
Residual and default-centered action targets feed effort-saturated PD control with zero desired joint velocity.

evidence.locator: Section II-D, Equations 7-9, and Appendix Table VI
evidence.claim: Mechanics-based gain equations, scaling, and exact joint-group actuation profiles are specified.
The MLP and temporal-convolution history encoder dimensions and normalization choices are stated.

evidence.locator: Section II-F and Appendix Table VII
evidence.claim: Nominal domain randomization and exact hand-force duration and cap are reported.

evidence.locator: Section II-G and Appendix Table VIII
evidence.claim: All variants share one specified reward, while reset sampling replays poorly tracked clips and phases more often with uniform coverage retained.
The motion split, actor-critic privileges, teacher-student sequence, environment count, iteration count, hardware, and approximate runtime are reported.
PPO and teacher-student optimization hyperparameters are tabulated.
The simulator cadence, held-out motions, initialization, no-perturbation condition, success rule, metric set, and aggregation order are fixed.
Absolute nominal errors and relative changes for every factor variant and TWIST2 are reported over 1,024 motions.
The stiffer fixed-scale profile has mixed tracking effects but increases maximum all-joint and upper-body torque by 13% and 41%.
The paper interprets each internal ablation and states that one additional training seed produced consistent trends without tabulating per-seed estimates.
TWIST2 is retrained on the same training motions and PPO iterations, then compared as an external complete pipeline under common metrics.
The same simulated checkpoint runs at 50 Hz without real-robot fine-tuning or command smoothing; pushes and soft-ground trials are presented qualitatively.
One controlled execution per policy reports steady-window elbow displacement under 1-6 kg hand loads and shows improved load holding with force randomization.
The 1.5 kg box lift is explicitly described as reference replay without box observation, adaptation, replanning, or autonomous manipulation.
One matched crouch phase shows larger torque peaks, ankle torque, and oscillation under the stiffer fixed-scale profile.
The authors identify the one-platform, one-factor-at-a-time scope and leave interactions and other humanoids untested.
